source.title: The Case for Full-Matrix Adaptive Regularization
source.authors: Naman Agarwal; Brian Bullins; Xin-Yi Chen; Elad Hazan; Karan Singh; Cyril Zhang; Yi Zhang

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Title in the supplied metadata differs slightly from the text title: metadata says “The Case for Full-Matrix Adaptive Regularization,” while the text says “Efficient Full-Matrix Adaptive Regularization.”
record.tranche_reason: Reports its own optimizer comparisons on image classification and language modeling. These refine V4: GGT, a full-matrix adaptive method, has task-dependent generalization relative to SGD and Adam; its results are not a simple optimizer-wide ordering.
record.gate_note: The paper compares GGT, Adam, AdaGrad and SGD and reports training and held-out metrics on CIFAR-10 and language-modeling tasks. Figure-only accuracy and perplexity curves are not transcribed as precise values. Cited findings from earlier work are not rows. Synthetic optimization results do not measure the generalization versions.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares adaptive optimizers with momentum SGD using held-out accuracy and perplexity, bearing on V4. It extends the comparison to full-matrix adaptation and additional architectures; it is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The central contribution is practical full-matrix adaptive preconditioning with convergence guarantees. Preliminary experiments show faster optimization, especially for recurrent language modeling, but no unconditional vision-task improvement; Adam beats GGT on the tested Transformer.
record.recipe_differences: Tests optimizer generalization using GGT, a full-matrix adaptive method, against SGD and diagonal adaptive optimizers. The paper does not test random-label memorization or the original versions' interventions and measures.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies by task and architecture: GGT improves validation perplexity over baselines on the LSTM character-level task, is outperformed by Adam on the Transformer, and does not improve CIFAR-10 generalization over SGD on the reported CNN settings. Learning-rate schedule also differs between the CIFAR-10 experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: GGT is competitive with Adam in word-level language modeling, with improvement confined to roughly the first 20 epochs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Full-matrix versus diagonal adaptive optimization has task-dependent benefits.

fits_no_version.finding: Adam eventually outperforms GGT in both training and validation loss on the Penn Treebank Transformer.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Full-matrix adaptive preconditioning does not consistently improve on diagonal adaptive optimization.

record.problems: Held-out results for several comparisons are shown only in plots and lack numerical uncertainty estimates. Optimizer conditions are not uniform across all experiments: the main residual CNN uses cosine annealing, while the VGG experiment uses a fixed halving schedule. The word-level result lacks a stated metric and model size.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying result rows left out; synthetic optimization curves and spectral plots do not measure the generalization versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and local connectivity.

Controlled limited-versus-broad tuning comparisons, decoupled weight decay, Adam-to-SGD switching, and word-level Adam-versus-SGD performance. The complete learning-rate search protocol is not specified.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Removal of memorized examples versus random removal.

missing.what: A sufficiently low learning rate improves training loss for any optimizer while worsening generalization by more than three percentage points. Record this tuning-sensitive result, distinguishing it from an adaptive-versus-SGD comparison.

Separate VGG19 results for Adam and AdaGrad are omitted. Appendix B.1 reports substantial training failure for diagonal adaptive methods, and Figure 6 includes their test-accuracy curves; their held-out comparisons with SGD need extraction from a readable figure.
missing.locator: Appendix B.1 and Figure 6, top panels

record.verdict_notes: Only the supplied text was used. Figure curves are not recoverable from their extracted axis labels. The study does not systematically compare tuning budgets, so its results establish optimizer orderings under the reported recipes rather than the causal effect of limited tuning.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label memorization or natural-label generalization comparison.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold comparison.
No convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparison.
No language benchmarks beyond the reported PTB settings; no broad optimizer tuning comparison, decoupled weight decay, or Adam-to-SGD switching.
No dropout ablation or comparison of explicit regularization.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or comparison of generalization measures.

rows.subject: SGD
rows.operation_detail: Trained the image classifier with SGD and momentum (parameter 0.9), cosine learning-rate annealing, and data augmentation; compared training loss and test accuracy with adaptive optimizers.

conditions.value: 4-pixel padding + random cropping and horizontal flipping

rows.value: Figure 3 (top) shows training loss and test accuracy curves; authors state SGD generalized slightly better than all other optimizers towards the end of training.
rows.note: Comparison result stated in text; the figure's precise accuracy values are not reported in text.
rows.check: The stated SGD advantage is small. SGD is an optimizer, not a model; the model is the residual network.

rows.subject: GGT
rows.operation_detail: Trained with the full-matrix adaptive optimizer GGT, momentum, cosine learning-rate annealing, and data augmentation; compared training loss and test accuracy with other optimizers.

conditions.value: 4-pixel padding + random cropping and horizontal flipping

rows.baseline: SGD, AdaGrad and Adam on the same task
rows.value: GGT consistently dominated existing optimizers in training loss; its test accuracy was below SGD near the end, with the stated gap < 0.2%.
rows.note: The text describes the training-loss ranking and the small held-out gap; it does not provide exact plotted accuracy values.
rows.check: Correct direction: GGT achieves better training loss but slightly worse test accuracy than SGD, with a reported gap below 0.2 percentage points. GGT is an optimizer.

rows.subject: Adam
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Adam and compared against GGT, AdaGrad and SGD on the CIFAR-10 image-classification task.

conditions.value: 4-pixel padding + random cropping and horizontal flipping

rows.baseline: SGD, AdaGrad and GGT on the same task
rows.value: Training loss and test accuracy are plotted in Figure 3 (top); no exact values or separate text ranking for Adam's test accuracy are stated.
rows.note: The text gives no Adam-specific held-out result; figure values are not reconstructed.
rows.check: The text explicitly says SGD generalizes slightly better than all other tested optimizers, which includes Adam. Exact plotted values are unnecessary to determine the direction. Adam is an optimizer.

rows.subject: AdaGrad
rows.operation_detail: Trained with AdaGrad and compared against GGT, Adam and SGD on the CIFAR-10 image-classification task.

conditions.value: 4-pixel padding + random cropping and horizontal flipping

rows.baseline: SGD, Adam and GGT on the same task
rows.value: Authors state AdaGrad's learning-rate decay is too aggressive, resulting in convergence to a poor solution; plotted test accuracy is not numerically reported.
rows.note: The poor-solution statement concerns convergence generally; no exact test-accuracy comparison is stated for AdaGrad.
rows.check: The explicit statement that SGD generalizes slightly better than all other optimizers supplies the held-out comparison. The separate poor-convergence statement does not establish better training performance for AdaGrad. AdaGrad is an optimizer.

rows.subject: GGT
rows.operation_detail: Trained with GGT for character-level language modeling and compared training and validation perplexity with Adam, AdaGrad and SGD.

conditions.value: 500 epochs for the cited final validation result

rows.note: The paper describes this as an end-to-end result competitive with reported recurrent-model results.
rows.check: For V4 the relevant comparator is SGD, not other adaptive optimizers: GGT's validation perplexity is 2.42 versus SGD's 2.76. This reverses the adaptive-disadvantage direction. GGT is an optimizer.

rows.subject: GGT
rows.operation_detail: Used GGT as a drop-in replacement for Adam in the cited word-level language-modeling code; compared performance with Adam.

conditions.value: first ∼20 epochs for the stated improvement

rows.value: Competitive with Adam; improvement observed only in the first ∼20 epochs.
rows.note: The paper does not state the model size or a named metric for this word-level experiment.
rows.check: GGT versus Adam compares two adaptive optimizers, with no SGD baseline or named held-out metric. It cannot test V4's adaptive-versus-SGD ordering. The supplied text does not establish a 3-layer, approximately 5M-parameter architecture for this experiment.

rows.subject: GGT
rows.operation_detail: Trained GGT and Adam on a Transformer for character-level language modeling; compared training and validation loss.
rows.value: After an initial lead, GGT was outperformed by Adam in training and validation loss.
rows.note: The stated outcome is a negative result for GGT relative to Adam; exact plotted perplexities are not stated.
rows.check: GGT versus Adam compares two adaptive optimizers without SGD. Adam's advantage is a valid result but does not establish V4's effect.

rows.subject: Adam
rows.operation_detail: Trained Adam and GGT on a Transformer for character-level language modeling; compared training and validation loss.
rows.value: Adam outperformed GGT in training and validation loss after GGT's initial lead.
rows.note: The text states the direction but provides no exact values.
rows.check: This is the reciprocal of R10's adaptive-versus-adaptive comparison, not evidence of an adaptive-versus-SGD advantage or disadvantage.

rows.subject: GGT
rows.operation_detail: Trained GGT on CIFAR-10 with a fixed halving learning-rate schedule; compared with SGD, AdaGrad and Adam.

conditions.value: 19-layer vanilla CNN without residual connections or batch normalization

rows.value: GGT stays on par with SGD throughout training, with a ∼1% generalization gap remaining at the end.
rows.note: The text does not spell out the direction of the ∼1% gap; it describes GGT as on par with SGD.
rows.check: The text reports similar training behavior and an approximately one-percentage-point generalization difference, but does not explicitly give its direction. The supplied figure text does not resolve it. GGT is an optimizer.

rows.subject: SGD
rows.operation_detail: Trained SGD on CIFAR-10 with a fixed halving learning-rate schedule; compared with GGT, AdaGrad and Adam.

conditions.value: 19-layer vanilla CNN without residual connections or batch normalization

rows.value: GGT stays on par with SGD throughout training; the paper reports a ∼1% generalization gap remaining at the end.
rows.note: The text does not spell out the direction of the ∼1% gap.
rows.check: This duplicates R12's comparison from the SGD side. Similar training behavior does not establish equal test accuracy, and the direction of the final generalization difference cannot be read from the supplied text.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10, Shake-Shake residual network, tuned learning rates with cosine annealing
relationships.reason: R1–R4 establish slightly better final test accuracy for SGD than for the adaptive optimizers; R2 additionally establishes better training loss for GGT.
relationships.display_finding: Reported final test accuracy slightly favored SGD over adaptive optimizers despite GGT's better training loss, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10, GGT with Shake-Shake regularization and tuned, annealed learning rates
relationships.reason: R1–R2 show an adaptive-versus-SGD accuracy gap below 0.2 percentage points; the authors attribute its reduced size to learning-rate tuning and strong explicit regularization.
relationships.display_finding: The reported accuracy gap below 0.2 percentage points under tuned learning rates and Shake-Shake regularization remains unverified.

relationships.condition: Penn Treebank character-level modeling with a 3-layer LSTM
relationships.reason: R5–R8 show all adaptive methods outperforming SGD: validation perplexities are 2.42 for GGT, 2.51 for Adam, 2.65 for AdaGrad, and 2.76 for SGD, extending the language-model exception beyond word-level modeling.
relationships.display_finding: Reported lower validation perplexity for GGT, Adam, and AdaGrad than SGD remains unverified.
